subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw core extend the existing package auto-updater into a scheduled, channel-notifying, consent-aware workflow, and which modes and safety guarantees should be part of that contract?
rationale: The missing work is feasible in core but crosses config, approval, unattended update execution, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and security policy boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Sponsor scoped core updater workflow
options.body: Define a default-off core contract for schedule/timezone, notify-only, confirm, silent, notification target, and post-restart reporting before splitting implementation into reviewed pieces.

options.title: Split prerequisites first
options.body: Keep this issue as an umbrella while external-updater, backup/rollback, post-update hook, and notification primitives are designed in narrower canonical items.

options.title: Defer beyond package auto-update
options.body: Keep the shipped package auto-updater as the supported core feature and decline the richer scheduled notification workflow for now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped core updater workflow
recommendation.body: Define a default-off core contract for schedule/timezone, notify-only, confirm, silent, notification target, and post-restart reporting before splitting implementation into reviewed pieces.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the core auto-updater and is the strongest product/history routing signal for the remaining update workflow boundary.
